note.headline: Dow and small caps lead as gold, copper and bitcoin all rise together
note.standfirst: The S&P 500 added 0.44% and breadth ran nearly two to one positive, with cyclicals and financials doing the work while megacap tech lagged. Gold rose 3.22% on the same day equities and bitcoin rallied, a combination that does not usually hold and is worth watching into next week.
takeaways: Breadth was broad and positive, 16 advancers to 9 decliners, with the Dow up 0.98% outpacing a flat-ish Nasdaq 100.
Financials led on GS +3.73% and MS +3.25%, while megacap tech stayed soft with NVDA -0.98% and AAPL -0.63%.
The curve bear steepened, 2s10s widened to 50bp, with the belly and long end up 4bp while the front end held.
Gold rallied 3.22% alongside risk assets, a divergence the risk barometer flags as its single largest drag on the score.
note.desk_view:
Today confirms the broad risk-on read: breadth 1.78 to 1, the Dow and Russell outpacing megacap tech, and VIX at its lowest print of the recent stretch. It contradicts a clean duration story, since the curve bear steepened with the belly and long end both up 4bp while breakevens stayed flat at 2.34%, meaning the move was real yield, not inflation. Credit's message was ambivalent: high yield firmed while investment grade sat at a session low, a split that argues against reading this as unambiguous credit strength.

The level that decides which story wins is the 10-year at 4.69%. If it holds or falls back, the equity rally can keep drawing on lower discount-rate optimism. If it pushes further into bear-steepening territory alongside a gold rally that persists, that combination stops looking like risk-on and starts looking like a term-premium and inflation-hedging trade wearing risk-on's clothes.
watching: Whether gold's rally alongside equities extends or reverses over the next session.
Whether the 10-year holds 4.69% or continues higher within the bear steepener.
Whether MOVE converges lower with VIX or the gap between rate and equity vol widens further.
Whether crypto's outperformance (BTC +6.61%, XRP +17.20%) holds or gives back into the next session.
note.equities:
The S&P 500 closed at 7674.37, up 0.44%. The Dow outpaced it at 53277.01, up 0.98%, and the Russell 2000 added 0.85% to 3017.87. The Nasdaq 100 lagged the pack at +0.33%, pulled down by megacap laggards: NVDA -0.98%, AAPL -0.63%, AMZN -0.57%. Materials led sector performance, XLB up 2.14%, with Health Care +1.29% and Consumer Discretionary +1.15% behind it. Utilities were the outlier, XLU down 2.29%, the sharpest sector move of the session in either direction.

Breadth confirmed the tape: 16 advancers against 9 decliners, a ratio of 1.78, with dispersion at 1.51. Single-name moves told a rotation story more than a tech story. TSLA led all names at +5.14%, followed by GS +3.73%, MS +3.25%, ORCL +3.10% and CRM +1.82%. The laggard list was shallow by comparison, none worse than NVDA's -0.98%. Financials and old-economy cyclicals did the heavy lifting while the AI complex sat this one out.
note.rates:
The curve bear steepened. 2s10s widened 4bp to 50bp, 3m10y added 3bp to 82bp, and 5s30s held flat at 84bp. The move was driven by the belly and long end: 5-year yields rose 4bp to 4.39%, 10-year rose 4bp to 4.69%, 30-year rose 4bp to 5.23%, while the 2-year held at 4.19% with no change on the day. That is a curve repricing higher term premium, not a front-end story.

Breakevens were static across the board: 5-year, 10-year and the 5y5y forward all sat at 2.34% with zero change, and 10-year TIPS held at 2.35%. No inflation signal from the rates market today, the move was a real-yield story. The 7-10 year Treasury proxy IEF fell 0.19% and printed among the session's lows, consistent with the belly selling off into the bear steepener.
note.credit: Credit was mixed and modest. Investment grade underperformed, LQD down 0.13% and sitting at a session low alongside Treasuries, while high yield firmed slightly, HYG +0.06% and JNK +0.10%. EM sovereign debt ticked up, EMB +0.05%, and leveraged loans added 0.05%. Long Treasuries fell harder than credit, TLT down 0.35%, underscoring that today's pressure sat in duration rather than spread. Tone in credit was steady, not stretched in either direction.
note.fx: The dollar index slipped 0.06% to 98.839, a quiet session for the greenback against a noisier cross-asset tape. EUR/USD rose 0.04% to 1.168 and GBP/USD added 0.35% to 1.365. USD/JPY rose 0.42% to 158.94, the yen weak even as risk assets rallied. AUD/USD was the G10 standout, up 0.70% to 0.717. In EM, USD/BRL fell 0.78% to 5.137 and USD/MXN fell 0.33% to 16.895, a session low for the pair, while USD/TRY held near its own highs at 48.03, down just 0.03% on the day.
note.commodities: Gold rose 3.22% to 4661.60, the loudest move in the commodity complex and one that sits oddly against a risk-on equity tape. Silver added 1.45% and platinum rose 3.30%. Industrial metals moved with equities: copper rose 1.86% to 6.58, aluminium rose 2.67%. Energy was split, WTI fell 1.36% to 86.64 while Brent held flat at +0.10%; natural gas rose 2.38%. Agriculture was volatile: corn rose 6.16% to a session high, wheat rose 2.53%, coffee fell 10.64%, and sugar edged to a fresh high on a 0.46% gain.
note.volatility: Equity vol came in hard. VIX fell 5.50% to 15.13 and VVIX fell 4.00% to 86.27, both consistent with the risk-on tape in equities. SKEW ticked up slightly to 143.9, a marginal bid for tail protection even as the broad vol level fell. Rate vol did not follow: MOVE rose 0.30% to 73.40, holding near its year-to-date highs while equity vol eased. That gap between equity and rate volatility is the more interesting signal from today's surface.
note.digital: Digital assets ran well ahead of the broader risk tape. Bitcoin rose 6.61% to 77859.23, Ether rose 8.05%, Solana rose 6.76%, and XRP led the group at +17.20%. The beta to risk was high today: crypto outperformed every other asset class in percentage terms, consistent with its contribution to the risk barometer, where BTC was the single largest positive input at +2.74.
note.international: Europe closed broadly higher and set the tone before New York opened: EURO STOXX 50 rose 0.63%, DAX rose 0.59%, FTSE rose 0.64%, and IBEX led at +0.76%. Asia was split, Hang Seng rose 1.21% and KOSPI rose 0.88%, while the Nikkei fell 0.30% and the ASX 200 fell 0.27%. The Americas outside the US were firm across the board, Bovespa +1.85%, Mexbol +2.14%, and the TSX closed at a fresh high, up 0.70%. New York inherited a session with more green than red globally, and traded in line with it.
note.correlation:
The standout cross-asset signal is the gold and equity rally happening on the same day. The risk barometer treats gold as a safe-haven signal, and its contribution to today's score was -1.97, by far the largest single drag, even as SPX contributed +0.62, RUT +0.87, copper +1.22, and BTC +2.74, all positive. That is not the usual pattern: gold typically falls when risk assets and copper rise together. Today it did not.

A second break sits in volatility. VIX fell 5.50% while MOVE rose 0.30%, meaning equity investors priced calm while rate markets did not. If gold keeps rallying alongside equities and rate vol stays elevated while equity vol falls, the standard cross-asset hedges, long gold against risk, long vol against duration, stop paying out the way they're supposed to. That would force a rethink of how this desk sizes protection, not just what it buys.
